title: spec draft: keep the role's raw report when the report shape check fails, and name its path in the error

sections.heading: Files
sections.body:
- `internal/engine/specdraft.go:201-384` (`removeFailedDraftReports`, `keepFailedDraftReport` and `RunSpecDraft`: preserve failed report text, clear old reports and return the path)
- `internal/engine/specdraft_test.go:104-196` (`TestSpecDraftTreeChangeNamesThePaths` harness and the four shape-report tests)
- `docs/design.md:401-429` (spec draft: what ork keeps on a shape failure)

sections.heading: Failing tests
sections.body:
All four tests are in `internal/engine/specdraft_test.go` and use the harness of `TestSpecDraftTreeChangeNamesThePaths` at line 104 (`specHarness(t)`, a `runner.script`, `SpecDraftConfig{Item: "S10", Dir: t.TempDir(), Lineup: one claude entry}`).
- TestSpecDraftShapeFailureKeepsTheReport: a fake role writes the same malformed report in both rounds. The report has `## Why`, `## Files` and so on (no `## Section` prefix) and a `## Owner needed` section, which is the S531 shape. `RunSpecDraft` fails with a `*ShapeError` after two rounds (the first and its resume). The error text names `Dir/spec-draft-failed-2.md`. `spec-draft-failed-1.md` and `spec-draft-failed-2.md` both exist and hold exactly the text the role wrote. Red today: no file is kept and the error has no path.
- TestSpecDraftShapeSuccessKeepsNoFailedReport: `Dir` already holds a stale `spec-draft-failed-1.md`. The role writes the valid `draftReport`. The draft succeeds and no `spec-draft-failed-*` file is left. Guard.
- TestSpecDraftShapeRetryThatPassesKeepsNoFailedReport: the role writes a malformed report in round 1 and `draftReport` in round 2 (the resume). The draft succeeds and no `spec-draft-failed-*` file is left. Guard.
- TestSpecDraftShapeFailureDropsFailedReportsOfAnOldDraft: `Dir` holds a stale `spec-draft-failed-3.md`. The role writes a malformed report in both rounds. The draft fails and the stale file is gone. Guard.

sections.heading: Implement
sections.body:
1. Write the four tests and see TestSpecDraftShapeFailureKeepsTheReport red for the stated reason (no kept file, no path in the error).
2. In `internal/engine/specdraft.go` add `removeFailedDraftReports(dir)`. It deletes `spec-draft-failed-*.md` in `Dir`, the same way `removeFailedSpecReports` does in `internal/engine/speccheck.go:249-254`.
3. Add `keepFailedDraftReport(dir string, n int, text string, err error) error`, modelled on `keepFailedSpecReport` (`internal/engine/speccheck.go:260-284`). When `err` is a `*ShapeError`, it writes `text` (mode 0600) to `Dir/spec-draft-failed-N.md` and returns a `*specShapeKept{Cause: shape, Path: path}` with no `Heads`, so the message ends `[report kept in PATH]`. If the write fails, or `err` is not a shape error, it returns `err` unchanged. Use the existing `specShapeKept` type and the existing path text.
4. In `RunSpecDraft`, call `removeFailedDraftReports(cfg.Dir)` once after the temp directory is made. Keep a local `failed` counter. At the shape check (`class == ExitOK` branch, now `specdraft.go:291`), keep `readSpecReport(reportPath, res.Report)` in a variable. When `ParseSpecDraft` fails on it, call `keepFailedDraftReport(cfg.Dir, failed+1, text, perr)`, count it on success, and use the returned error as `problem`. Do this before the `os.Remove(reportPath)` of the resume at `specdraft.go:310`. The nudge text keeps using the plain shape error (`perr.Error()`), so the role does not see a path. A resume or the final `return nil, problem` then carries the path.
5. After the final `ParseSpecDraft(text)` succeeds, call `removeFailedDraftReports(cfg.Dir)`, so the files mean the last draft failed. Do not change what `ParseSpecDraft` accepts or its problem texts.
6. Docs: in `docs/design.md` (spec draft paragraph, `docs/design.md:408-412`), add a *Proposed (S576)* sentence. A report that fails its shape is kept as `spec-draft-failed-N.md` in the draft's directory (`spec-checks/<project-key>/<item-key>/draft/`, N counts the failed reports of this draft from 1). The error ends with `[report kept in PATH]`. A new draft removes the old failed reports, and a draft that passes removes its own.
7. Changelog: `slicer changelog add S576 --text "..."`. Do not edit `CHANGELOG.md`.

sections.heading: Check
sections.body:
Acceptance criteria:
- A spec draft whose report fails its shape twice leaves spec-draft-failed-1.md and spec-draft-failed-2.md in the draft directory, each holding the report the role wrote. The error ends with [report kept in PATH] for the second file.
- A spec draft that passes, including one that passes on its resume, leaves no spec-draft-failed-* file. A new draft removes the failed reports of an old one.
- What ParseSpecDraft accepts does not change: go test -run TestSpecDraftReportParsesOneBlockPerSection ./internal/engine still passes.

Commands:
- `go test -run TestSpecDraftShapeFailureKeepsTheReport ./internal/engine` passes (red before the change).
- `go test -run TestSpecDraftShapeSuccessKeepsNoFailedReport ./internal/engine` passes.
- `go test -run TestSpecDraftShapeRetryThatPassesKeepsNoFailedReport ./internal/engine` passes.
- `go test -run TestSpecDraftShapeFailureDropsFailedReportsOfAnOldDraft ./internal/engine` passes.
- `go test -run TestSpecDraftReportParsesOneBlockPerSection ./internal/engine` passes.
- `go test ./...` passes.
- `go vet ./...` prints nothing.
- `gofmt -l .` prints nothing.
- `slicer check` exits 0.
- [HUMAN CHECK] [AFTER LAND] The next time ork spec draft ork ID --json fails with report shape: ..., the error ends with [report kept in .../draft/spec-draft-failed-2.md], and that file holds what the role wrote, so you can see why no block was found.
